data.title: Remote Command-Execution Channel
data.summary: The sample accepts and executes arbitrary commands issued by the operator over its C2 channel, giving interactive-equivalent control without a full remote-access GUI.
data.description:
This is the command-execution half of a C2 relationship, distinct from the transport
carrying it (see application-layer C2 protocol): a received command is passed to a local
command interpreter and the output returned over the same channel, giving the operator
de facto shell access scoped only by the malware's own privilege level. The command set
exposed — a handful of fixed functions versus a full arbitrary-shell passthrough —
indicates how much capability the sample was built to support versus how much was left to
the operator's own tooling once a shell is available.
data.recommendation:
* Capture the command set and any observed command traffic; it directly indicates the operator's actual objective on this host, separate from the sample's static capability list.
* Where arbitrary shell passthrough is confirmed, treat the host as fully compromised at the privilege level the sample runs with, not merely 'infected'.
* Hunt for a parent-child relationship between the C2 process and a command interpreter it spawned, as a detection signal independent of the specific commands sent.
data.short_recommendation: Capture observed command traffic; it indicates the operator's actual objective on this host, beyond the sample's static capability.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Passed received command strings directly to cmd.exe via CreateProcess and returned the captured output over the C2 channel.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Forwarded received commands to a local shell interpreter and relayed its output back over the existing channel.
